reading_text: The birch stands bare against grey light, then one branch shows green while the ground beneath it stays cold. Soon the whole tree carries small leaves, though nothing was warm enough for it. Berkana is that opening that comes before its season, quiet and early. Was there a green you noticed then, or one you only see now looking back?

The fog rolls in off the fjord and swallows the far shore whole. This is Blank, Anna, the not-yet-seen that keeps its own hour and shows you only the water at your feet. You stand at the edge, and the mist does not lift on asking.

The door stands open, Anna, and the second cup waits where a hand has not yet reached it. Gebo is that warmth held ready between two people, given and received in one motion. The steam still rises, and there is no hurry in the waiting.

You walk the long road home, and far off a single light burns in the window, held there by someone who would not sleep until you arrived. Algiz is that watch kept for you while you were away. Whichever turn the road takes, the light stays lit.

The egg lies whole in the nest, warm, holding everything and showing none of it. This is Ingwaz, the season before the season, all of it kept quiet under one still shell. Whatever you were becoming then, it was already there, unbroken.

The voice on the line, Anna, says the thing at last, and the words become a road opening where a moment ago there was only waiting. Ansuz is that turn from silence into speech, the air carrying what could not be seen. You stand now with the phone still warm in your hand.

The coffee sits untouched, the steam long gone from its surface. This is Isa, the pause that holds two people in place while neither reaches across the table. The cup stays where it was set, cold and full.

Two horses climb the ridge together, matching each other stride for stride, neither pulling ahead nor falling behind. This is Ehwaz, the quiet trust that lets two carry one pace up hard ground. What lies ahead asks not for speed but for that same keeping-together. The path narrows, and still the two hooves fall in time.

The loaf splits open at the crust, and the warmth held inside meets the cooler air of the room. Fehu is that warmth handed across a table, more than one pair of hands can hold alone. What you keep back stays warm only for a while, what you pass on feeds two. You stand at the table with the bread still steaming before you.

You step in from the cold, and the door closing behind you turns the sharp air into something that holds you. Someone lit the stove before you came, and the warmth was already waiting. Wunjo is that ease of being met, the room made ready by another hand. You stand just inside, the cold still on your coat, the heat reaching you.

Behind the bright field, the hour is late and everyone should be sleeping. Sowilo is that light that stays up warming what grows long after the day was done. Something between two people kept giving warmth past the point you thought it had ended. You stand in that hayfield, Anna, in a brightness the clock says should have gone.

Behind the door those keys once turned, the house has settled into other hands, other footsteps warming the boards. Othila is that quiet loosening of a grip on what was yours, the keys still cool in your palm though the lock no longer answers them. What was home stays behind you, small now against the wider ground ahead. You stand at the gate with your hand open.

Behind the last cairn you can see lies another you cannot, though the builders placed it there all the same. This is Raidho, each stone raised close enough to catch the next through fog. You stand at one marker, the one before it still in sight.

The bowl on the counter holds still while the dough beneath the cloth swells at its own pace. Jera is that slow rising you cannot press faster with your hands. You may want the way ahead settled tonight, but the proof comes when it comes, not when you knock on the bowl. You stand at the counter, waiting on what the warmth is already doing.

A single midge touches the lagoon and the whole mirrored sky shivers, the water that held every cloud so plainly now broken. Mannaz is how you came to see your own work clearly, once the surface stilled. That knowing was never the still water, Anna, it was the settling.

Where the black rock meets the green, the moss has crept over stone that once ran molten. Uruz is that slow turning, heat spent into something that holds and stays. The old fire is still down there, cooled now under a soft skin of grey-green. You walk across ground that has already changed shape.
